solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Guitarist running after two men in a boat

indicators.note: after says the word for running comes behind the two names

parts.note: George and Harris are two of the three men in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A guitarist dashing along behind a couple of men out rowing.
explanation.walkthrough: Three Men in a Boat (1889) is a classic English comic novel about J, George and Harris on the Thames; two of them supply the first names.
explanation.definitionFit: George Harrison was the lead guitarist of the Beatles.

clue.text: Massive jar contains shelled peas for foodie

parts.note: something massive is epic in scale

indicators.note: contains says the jar holds the next letters within it

parts.note: an urn is a large jar or vase

indicators.note: shelled strips the outer letters off the word peas, as pods come off peas

explanation.surface: A huge jar holding podded peas is a gift for a food lover.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is a person devoted to refined eating and drinking, a gourmet.

clue.text: A Christian cycling waves

indicators.note: cycling says the letters go round, the last one moving to the front

parts.note: Christian Dior, the French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A Christian on a bike waving to passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the R of ADIOR from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio is broadcasting by electromagnetic waves, so 'the waves' can stand for it.

clue.text: U-boat ends manoeuvres on a bearing of 90°

indicators.note: manoeuvres means the letters of the following words are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A submarine finishes its manoeuvres heading due east.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass bearing of 90 degrees points due east, so travelling on it is heading east.

clue.text: A Scot telephoned the FT, seeing no leader

indicators.note: seeing no leader says the first letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: telephoned is rang, and the FT, speaking of itself, is us

explanation.surface: A Scotsman rang the Financial Times, but couldn't see the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appears in the FT, so 'the FT' is the paper referring to itself as US.
explanation.definitionFit: Angus is a typical Scottish male first name, so an Angus is a Scot.

clue.text: Switch behind cooker

parts.note: behind, the backside, is the rear
a range is a large kitchen cooker

explanation.surface: A switch round the back of the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch things about is to rearrange them, changing their order.

clue.text: Get drunk then take drugs

parts.note: so, as in 'and so', means then
to use is slang for taking drugs

explanation.surface: A wild night out: drinking first, then drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To souse is to drench, and soused is slang for drunk, so souse is to get drunk.

clue.text: Sewers drained Newcastle and fouled Leeds

indicators.note: drained empties the word Newcastle, leaving only its outside letters
fouled means the letters of Leeds are messed up into another order

explanation.surface: Drains in two northern cities are emptied and blocked: Newcastle and Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' is not drains but things that sew, pronounced like 'sowers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles are the tools that sew, so they are sewers in the stitching sense.

clue.text: Caught entering booby-trapped ground

indicators.note: entering says the letter for caught goes inside the other word

parts.note: ground that is booby-trapped has been mined
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is caught stepping onto mined ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like the noun land, but it is the past participle of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced meat has been ground up finely, so minced means ground.

clue.text: Long poem that sounds like a coffee commercial?

indicators.note: that sounds like says the answer is said the same as the phrase

parts.note: Illy is an Italian coffee brand, so an advert for it is an Illy ad

explanation.surface: An epic poem that's really just an advert for coffee?
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Iliad is a long epic poem about the Trojan War.

clue.text: Personal authority is about good character

indicators.note: about says the word is is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: a person's nature is their character

explanation.surface: A man's own authority depends on his good character.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature is a person's own mark that authorises a document.

clue.text: French physicist runs out of clubroom in a tizzy

indicators.note: in a tizzy, flustered and confused, says the remaining letters are jumbled
out of says that letter leaves the word clubroom

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A French scientist storms out of the clubroom in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R from CLUBROOM, and 'in a tizzy' rearranges the remaining CLUBOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb was the French physicist after whom the unit of electric charge is named.

clue.text: Observe what someone pulling pints does when told?

indicators.note: when told says the phrase is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a barman pulling pints serves ale

explanation.surface: A riddle about the job of a barman.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulling pints means drawing beer from a hand pump in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To surveil is to keep someone under close watch, to observe them.

clue.text: Test out of ten given by doctor for vision

indicators.note: given by says the doctor's letters come first
out of says the ten leaves the word for test

parts.note: an exam is a test
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: An eye test, marks out of ten, from a doctor checking vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a vision seen in sleep, or a vision of what one hopes for.

clue.text: Spanish chap punched by total monster

indicators.note: punched by says the word for chap is broken into by the others

parts.note: a chap is a man
all means the total
an orc is a fantasy monster

explanation.surface: A Spaniard thumped by a complete brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish chap' looks like the definition, but only 'Spanish' defines; 'chap' gives MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallorcan describes things from Mallorca, an island belonging to Spain.

clue.text: Sort of characters to spurn dale?

definitions.text: Sort of characters to spurn dale?

indicators.note: sort of characters says the letters that follow are sorted into a different order

explanation.surface: What kind of people would shun a valley?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: hill-dwellers are those who would spurn the dale.
explanation.definitionFit: Uplanders live in high country, so they are the sort who would turn their back on a valley.

clue.text: Sparkling red coral starts to bleach making scientists upset at sea

indicators.note: at sea, all confused, says the letters are jumbled together
starts to picks the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Bleached coral reefs worry marine scientists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes B, M, S and U, and 'at sea' mixes them with CORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is an Italian red wine that is usually lightly sparkling.

clue.text: Eg Marx once made funny duck film

indicators.note: made funny says the letters of once are made odd, rearranged

parts.note: a duck, a score of nothing in cricket, is O
a mist is a thin film of moisture

explanation.surface: Groucho Marx made a funny film, Duck Soup.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Groucho and the Marx Brothers' film Duck Soup; the definition is Karl Marx.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx wrote Das Kapital and was an economist, among other things.

clue.text: Carol meets professional beauty on the rebound, having no partner

parts.note: to carol is to sing

indicators.note: on the rebound says the word bounces back, reading right to left

parts.note: a model is someone paid for their looks

explanation.surface: Carol takes up with a model after a breakup, being single.
explanation.definitionFit: Singledom is the state of being unattached, without a romantic partner.

clue.text: Type that is wearing glasses

indicators.note: wearing says the glasses go round the other letters, as worn

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: That's the sort of person who wears glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or sort, so a type.

clue.text: Music business divided by Simpson's yellow face, perhaps

indicators.note: divided by says the music company is split by the other letters

parts.note: EMI is a British record company
OJ is O. J. Simpson, the American footballer

explanation.surface: A recording company split over a yellow Simpsons character.
explanation.walkthrough: The Simpsons are drawn yellow, but the Simpson here is O. J.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic smiley emoji is a yellow face, one example of the many symbols.

clue.text: Classified as bound by Darwin's ideas

indicators.note: bound by says the answer is held within the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of Darwin's into the start of ideas

explanation.surface: Something secret contained in Darwin's theories.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside information is privileged and secret, as classified material is.

clue.text: In retreat, some of foe's aeroplanes slow down

indicators.note: In retreat says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the enemy's planes pull back and slow down.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to reduce speed or effort, to slacken.

clue.text: Stay in charge having lost power, unmoved

indicators.note: having lost says the letter for power is taken away

parts.note: to stop is to stay, as in stopping overnight
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: Remaining in command after losing power, impassive.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic person bears hardship calmly, showing no emotion.

clue.text: Offer to sell stock in empty apartment?

indicators.note: in says the empty letter goes inside the word for apartment

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
O, a zero, stands for nothing, empty

explanation.surface: Should you sell shares in an unoccupied flat?
explanation.definitionFit: To float a company is to offer its shares for sale to the public for the first time.

clue.text: Noisy place for a carnival, as we call it

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro holds the famous carnival
to us means in our opinion, as we see it

explanation.surface: A noisy carnival venue, as we'd describe it.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotous behaviour is loud and unruly.

clue.text: Prison camp belonging to prisoner

parts.note: of means belonging to, as in 'the house of John'
lag is British slang for a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A camp holding a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: An oflag was a German prisoner-of-war camp for officers in the Second World War.

clue.text: Interior gutted immediately after mad decoration

indicators.note: gutted removes the insides of the word interior, leaving its ends

parts.note: on means immediately after, as in 'on arrival'
cross means angry, mad

explanation.surface: A decorator gutted the interior and was furious.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a German military medal, a decoration for bravery.

clue.text: Glen's big cheese left dairy unfinished and runny

indicators.note: runny says the letters run about, rearranged
unfinished says the last letter of dairy is dropped

explanation.surface: A local bigwig leaves a soft, runny cheese from the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' leaves DAIR, and 'runny' rearranges it. A laird is a Scottish landowner, fitting a glen, a Scottish valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird owns a Scottish estate, making him the important person, the big cheese, of a glen.

clue.text: Cold feet while wearing support tights inside out

parts.note: to second a proposal is to support it
while can mean though, as in 'while wearing tights, he...' meaning 'though he wore'

indicators.note: inside out says the inner letters of tights are taken out, leaving the ends

explanation.surface: Getting cold feet while wearing tights that are on inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside out' takes the inner letters out of TIGHTS, leaving TS; 'while wearing' reads loosely as THOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Second thoughts are doubts about a decision, the idiom 'cold feet'.
